flags.why: The Vietnamese does not say the two men are friends, and “Anh” here refers to the speaker or addressee rather than an unrelated third person.
flags.fix: You and he married two sisters, so you are brothers-in-law.

flags.why: This term is mainly Northern Vietnamese, as noted under the regional equivalents in [Wiktionary](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/anh_em_c%E1%BB%8Dc_ch%C3%A8o).
“Đồng đều” means equal or even, without implying fairness or equity, as defined in the [Vietnamese dictionary](https://loigiaihay.com/tu-dien-tv/dong-deu-eqPfpp7Gop7LA.html).
